Topic: Fundamental Constants and Mathematical Structure in Turbulence

Target audience: Advanced undergraduate physics/engineering students

Section: section_1 — Introduction: The Chaos in the Fluid

Lecture lines:
Turbulence is an energy cascade of chaotic fluid motion.
Inertial forces dominate at high velocities.
Viscous forces eventually dampen the flow motion.

Planned animations:
Show chaotic fluid motion as a field of swirling vectors.
Fade in label 'Turbulence' with color #FF5733.
Show particles dispersing rapidly.
Highlight 'Dissipation' area with soft glow color #33FF57.
Morph vectors into simplified turbulent eddies.

Section: section_2 — The Kolmogorov Hypotheses (1941)

Lecture lines:
Energy cascades from large scales to small.
Small-scale turbulence is isotropic and universal.
Governed by dissipation rate and viscosity.

Planned animations:
Display Kolmogorov's name with date '1941' at top.
Show large scale energy input as a swirling vortex.
Animate energy transfer through smaller eddies via cascading.
Display 'Energy Cascade' label in #33A1FF.
Show energy reaching dissipation scale and fading.

Section: section_3 — Mathematical Structure: The Energy Spectrum

Lecture lines:
Energy follows the Kolmogorov -5/3 spectrum.
Wavenumber k relates to eddy scale size.
The spectrum shows power density versus wavenumber.
Energy cascades down across these scales.
This structure reveals underlying mathematical order.

Planned animations:
Write spectral energy formula E(k) on screen.
Animate curve representing E(k) proportional to k^-5/3.
Highlight k^-5/3 term with color #F1C40F.

Section: section_4 — The Kolmogorov Length Scale (η)

Lecture lines:
Viscosity turns kinetic energy into heat.
Eta is the smallest turbulence length scale.
Formula: η equals ν cubed over ε.

Planned animations:
Display length scale η as a small dot.
Show η formula: η = (ν^3/ε)^1/4.
Highlight the exponent 1/4 with flashing #E74C3C color.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Real-world Application

Lecture lines:
Energy enters large and dissipates at η.
Constants enable modeling without tracking atoms.
Turbulence models help design efficient systems.

Planned animations:
Display atmospheric turbulence vs pipe flow side by side.
Summarize K41 utility with a checkmark icon in #2ECC71.
Fade out all with a summary message 'Understanding Chaos'.

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
